sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Double-Shot PBT Plastic Injection of Novelty Keyboard Keycaps

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (Aolepān Aorōkin Ṃajeḷ)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – predominantly Common Law (US-derived, modeled on Delaware General Corporation Law and ABA Model Business Corporation Act) with customary law overlay
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States (1986, Amended 2003)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) / PACER-Plus (2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, as amended; Criminal Code 2011 (money laundering and terrorist financing offenses); Business Corporations Act 1990 (B.C.A.), as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) supervisory directives; AML/CFT National Risk Assessment (in force under APG obligations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (with certified copy for apostille)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Competent Authority: Office of the Attorney General, Majuro) or, for non-Hague destinations, consular legalization at the RMI Consulate/Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (post-incorporation), if required by opening bank or key supplier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized corporate resolutions / statutory declaration of beneficial ownership (if required by foreign bank or e-commerce payment rail)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI-licensed notary public or licensed registered agent (in-country notarization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated sanctions list, UK OFAC/OFIS-equivalent listings, and the RMI FIU watchlist, with immediate freeze-and-suspicious-transaction-reporting obligations under the 2018 AML/CFT Act; PEPs require enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Title 27, Marshall Islands Revised Code); Articles of Incorporation filed under Section 23; registered office and registered agent under Section 33; Board powers, By-Laws and officer provisions under Sections 40-50.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Corporate Registry, Majuro); all submissions effected through a licensed RMI Registered Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (in English), executed by each incorporator and acknowledged/notarized, delivered to the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Authorized capital is fixed in the Articles of Incorporation; shares may be issued for such consideration as determined by the Board, with par value per share stated in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby approves the subscription of the initial subscribers to [●] shares of Common Stock, par value US$[●] per share, in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation, and authorizes the President to issue and deliver share certificates upon receipt of full consideration; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation at [●], Majuro, Marshall Islands, together with [●] as registered agent, is adopted and shall be continuously maintained; RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed President, [●] Secretary, and [●] Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board until a successor is appointed; and RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file all statutory returns in the ordinary course.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RMI Registrar of Corporations (Corporate Registry, Majuro) via licensed RMI Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-clearance inquiry and name-reservation application to the Registrar through the appointed RMI Registered Agent. The proposed name must contain a corporate designator ('Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or an accepted abbreviation). The Registrar reserves an available name for up to 30 days and issues a reservation confirmation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Identity and address particulars of the incorporator(s)
Registered Agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict with an existing or reserved name, submit up to three alternate names within five business days or request administrative review of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators (signatories) and a notary public authorized in the jurisdiction of signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation to include: (i) corporate name; (ii) registered office address within the Republic of the Marshall Islands; (iii) name of the resident registered agent; (iv) statement of purpose covering any lawful business, including ISIC 3240 manufacturing of mechanical keyboard keycaps; (v) authorized capital structure (number of shares and par value); and (vi) any permitted limitations. Each incorporator executes the Articles, and signatures are acknowledged before a notary public prior to delivery to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Signed Consent to Act as Registered Agent (RMI-licensed agent)
Statement of authorized shares (where included in Articles)
Power of attorney in favor of the submitting agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon receipt of a deficiency notice from the Registrar, correct the specified particulars and resubmit within 30 days; the instrument takes effect on the date filed or such later date as stated therein.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the RMI Registered Agent, deliver the executed Articles of Incorporation to the Registrar together with the US$250 statutory filing fee (plus the registered agent's professional fee). Upon acceptance, the Registrar files the Articles, records the Certificate of Incorporation, and issues the certificate evidencing creation of the Business Corporation with separate legal personality and limited liability.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (signed original)
Registered Agent Consent to Act
Filing fee payment confirmation (wire or ACH remittance)
Registered Agent cover letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Expedited processing (same-day or 24-hour) is available for an additional statutory fee; if the filing is rejected, refile within the Registrar's stated cure period (typically 30 days) without losing the original filing date unless otherwise determined by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RMI-licensed Registered Agent appointed by the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the permanent registered office at the physical address of the RMI Registered Agent in Majuro. The registered agent maintains business hours, receives official correspondence and service of process on behalf of the Corporation, and files the registered agent consent with the Registrar. The acceptance letter and registered office confirmation are retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Registered Agent Acceptance/Consent Form
Registered Office Confirmation Letter
Standard Corporate Services Agreement with the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or ceases to satisfy the licensed-agent requirements, appoint a successor and file a Notice of Change of Registered Agent with the Registrar within 30 days to avoid administrative dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolutions, Share Issuance and Banking Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (acting by unanimous written consent or at an inaugural meeting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting. The Board: (i) adopts the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (approving share subscription, registered office/agent, and officer appointments); (ii) adopts the By-Laws of the Corporation; (iii) authorizes the issuance of share certificates and the maintenance of the stock ledger; and (iv) authorizes officers to open bank and payment-rail accounts (including Shopify Payments and Stripe settlement accounts) and execute KYC and banking resolutions.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution (or unanimous written consent)
Adopted By-Laws
Share certificates and stock ledger
Bank account opening, KYC and beneficial-ownership forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment-acquirer or bank due diligence requests further corporate evidence, provide certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation and First Board Resolution, with apostille from the RMI Registrar where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Registration, Good Standing and Tax-Exempt Status Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RMI Registrar of Corporations; RMI Revenue and Taxation Office (advisory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual registration statement and pay the minimum annual registration fee (US$100, plus any registered agent service fee) to maintain good standing. As a non-resident Business Corporation deriving no income from sources within the Marshall Islands, the entity is exempt from RMI income tax, capital gains tax and withholding tax. No business license under the RMI Business License Act is required where no physical office or local sales activity is conducted in the RMI.
required_dossiers: Annual registration statement
Current officer and director register (if changed)
Proof of annual registration fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the entity is struck off for non-payment, apply for reinstatement under the Registrar's restoration procedure within the applicable period upon payment of arrears and any penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: RMI Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA) - advisory only; no industrial license is mandated for the non-resident, tax-exempt Business Corporation conducting offshore manufacturing of double-shot PBT keyboard keycaps.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable to the non-resident entity. Contingent: Manufacturing/Industrial Operating License under the RMI Business License Act (1991) and an RMI EPA environmental permit would be required only if a physical injection-molding facility were established inside the Marshall Islands.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA), constituted under the National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) 1984 (as amended).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Contingent advisory: a plastic injection-molding facility for keycap production would be classified as an NEPA Category II (Preliminary Environmental Review) or Category III (full Environmental Impact Assessment) project if established in the RMI; no EIA applies to the current offshore/contract-manufacturing model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Contingent compliance thresholds for any RMI-based facility: wastewater discharge free of visible sheen and within pH 6.0-8.5; no free-floating oil/grease; VOC emissions within RMI clean-air limits; and segregation/disposal of plastic scrap, pigment and packaging waste in accordance with NEPA hazardous and solid waste requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Contingent advisory: any physical RMI premises would require fire-safety certification from the Majuro Fire Department and RMI National Disaster Management Office, structural load inspection, and occupational clearance under RMI occupational safety and health rules (machine guarding for injection-molding presses, PPE, noise control, electrical safety). Not applicable to the offshore manufacturing model.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance (Tax and Customs Division / Office of the Chief Collector of Taxes); portal: n/a — no general e-filing or online tax portal exists for non-resident exempt corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation registered under the Business Corporations Act is not automatically assigned a Marshall Islands corporate tax identification number. Registration is effective with the Registrar of Corporations. A TIN is issued only upon written application to the Ministry of Finance if the entity later engages in local economic activities requiring income tax, import duty, social security, or withholding registration. No tax clearance certificate is required for offshore formation or maintenance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available. The non-resident Business Corporation enjoys a statutory, non-elective exemption from Marshall Islands income tax provided it does not carry on a local trade or business. No check-the-box, pass-through election, hybrid mismatch election, or analogous tax classification regime exists under Marshall Islands law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax is levied in the Marshall Islands. Import duty applies only to physical importation of goods into the customs territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No threshold applicable — VAT/GST registration does not exist. Import duty liability arises per shipment, not through economic turnover. Local statutory currency is the U.S. dollar (USD); threshold: N/A.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or digital stamping requirement is in force. Invoices are commercial records used only for customs valuation; no real-time tax clearance platform exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Because the Marshall Islands imposes no VAT or GST, exports of goods and the supply of offshore services to clients outside the Marshall Islands fall entirely outside the scope of indirect taxation. No zero-rating claim, export registration, or VAT refund mechanism exists or is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: None required for tax substantiation — no export VAT/GST refund regime exists in the Marshall Islands.
Customs outward manifest or shipping bill may be required by the Customs Act for departure control/statistical purposes when goods leave an RMI port.
Commercial invoice may be requested by customs for valuation purposes, but it is not a tax refund or zero-rating document.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No Marshall Islands VAT/GST export zero-rating or refund framework exists, so no tax-specific clawback or penalty can be asserted. Fraudulent misrepresentation, false customs declarations, or forged shipping documents nonetheless remain subject to general criminal penalties under the Crimes Act and Customs Act, which may include fines and/or imprisonment; no indirect-tax-specific retrospective clawback is prescribed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Division of Financial Institutions Supervision, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands — the RMI has no domestic central bank, no sovereign currency, and has adopted the U.S. dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains full convertibility for both capital-account and current-account transactions. There are no exchange-control statutes restricting inward equity, shareholder loans, trade settlement, dividend distribution, or profit repatriation. The U.S. dollar is the operating currency, so no local-currency conversion event arises. Profit remittance is not subject to FX approval or RMI withholding tax for a non-resident Business Corporation; the only practical hurdles are bank-level AML/KYC, beneficial-ownership verification, U.S. OFAC sanctions screening, and evidence of the underlying commercial substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. RMI law imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export receipts to an RMI-licensed bank. For the custom mechanical keyboard cap e-commerce business, export receipts collected through Shopify Payments, Stripe, or other payment processors may remain in USD in any supported settlement account or may be swept to the RMI Business Corporation's licensed bank account without any surrender or conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Direct use of Shopify Payments and Stripe is not supported for a merchant incorporated in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, as neither processor lists RMI as a supported country. Feasibility is Medium through a U.S. or Hong Kong merchant-of-record arrangement or through a licensed foreign EMI such as Payoneer, Airwallex, or Currenxie, provided the RMI Business Corporation retains a compliant licensed bank account as the ultimate treasury settlement point. RMI law does not issue standalone EMI licences to fintechs, and unlicensed custodianship of customer funds inside RMI would raise Banking Act concerns; therefore all processor and EMI balances should be swept on a daily basis to the licensed bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI banks generally require a physical or supervised video-identity verification of at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner before opening a non-resident corporate account. In-person attendance at the Majuro branch is the baseline; remote opening may be accepted only where the signatory already has an existing bank relationship or where the bank agrees to video KYC under its internal AML/CFT policy. For a foreign-owned Business Corporation, certified corporate documents, an apostilled board resolution, passport copies, and a fully completed UBO register are mandatory. A signatory without physical RMI presence will typically face enhanced due diligence and may be asked to appear before a notary or RMI consular officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-owned non-resident Business Corporation with no office, no employees, and no physical economic substance in RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing; certified articles of incorporation and bylaws; registered agent certificate; board resolution authorizing account opening; register of directors and shareholders; ultimate beneficial ownership declaration; commercial operating agreements; supplier purchase orders; customer export invoices; warehouse or 3PL contract; domain and website ownership evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of nominee directors or corporate service provider addresses that obscure the actual beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Nominee director declaration disclaiming beneficial interest; signed corporate service agreement; complete UBO identification with notarized passport copies; residential address proof; source of wealth documentation; group organization chart; shareholder loan and equity contribution records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid high-volume e-commerce deposits from pooled Shopify or Stripe settlement accounts where the bank cannot trace end-customer transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements with Shopify and Stripe; settlement statements matched to order numbers; per-order commercial invoices; shipping and tracking logs; customs declarations; refund and chargeback policy; PCI DSS attestation; reconciliation reports linking platform payouts to bank credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or shareholder loan amount disproportionate to the stated tooling, raw-material, and inventory requirements of the keyboard keycap business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions approving the capital injection; updated share register; signed shareholder loan agreement; SWIFT Field 70 purpose code stating 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN'; cash-flow forecast for PBT/ABS resin, molds, double-shot injection tooling, packaging, and fulfillment; management accounts or audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent bank concern that the RMI entity is a mere conduit for moving funds between unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete order-to-cash documentation; Shopify/Stripe business dashboard summaries; fulfillment center contracts; customer communications; purchase history; tax-exempt certificate and annual corporate registry filings; AML/CFT policy statement and designated compliance officer contact.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject equity or shareholder loans exclusively via SWIFT MT103 USD wire from a bank account owned by the injecting shareholder to the RMI Business Corporation's operational account at Bank of Guam – Majuro Branch or Bank of Marshall Islands. The remittance message must identify the ordering customer, the beneficiary account as the RMI entity, and include Field 70 with 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – [ENTITY NAME] – BOARD RESOLUTION [DATE]' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN – [LOAN AGREEMENT DATE]'. No RMI exchange-control approval is required; the receiving bank will verify sanctions status, source of funds, and beneficial ownership. If the remitting jurisdiction requires a formal purpose code, the remitting bank should use the BPM6 code for direct investment equity or shareholder loan rather than a goods-trade code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlement of keycap raw materials and logistics, use SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers from the RMI entity's USD account, or a UCP600-compliant commercial letter of credit issued by Bank of Guam or Bank of Marshall Islands when the supplier requires documentary payment security. The payment file should reference supplier invoice number, contract number, Incoterms (CIF, FOB, EXW), and transport documents. Because RMI uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender, settlement is naturally closed in USD; any non-USD payments such as CNY, TWD, or EUR should be converted through a foreign correspondent account using the hedging instruments below, and the full trade document trail must be retained for bank audit and AML/CFT review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore plain-vanilla FX forwards (USD/CNY, USD/TWD, USD/EUR) executed through an OECD-regulated international dealing bank to fix the USD cost of non-USD supplier invoices.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted currencies such as CNY and TWD, arranged by an international bank acting as calculation agent, because no onshore RMI FX forward market exists.
Cross-currency swaps for matched balance-sheet hedging when non-USD payable exposure exceeds USD 5 million, permitted as OTC derivatives through an OECD-licensed dealer with board authorization.

Natural hedging by denominating all sales, raw-material, and logistics contracts in USD and maintaining USD-only clearing accounts; this is the preferred treasury policy given the absence of a domestic RMI exchange market.
Forward rate agreements or interest-rate swaps only when linked to a documented third-party commercial loan; otherwise disfavored for this low-risk e-commerce business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Franchise Tax Payment (Business Corporation Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year, covering the preceding calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing and late-payment penalty of USD 100 is imposed after 31 March. Continued default may result in administrative dissolution or revocation of corporate standing after formal delinquency notice, with reinstatement conditioned on payment of all outstanding fees, penalties, and reinstatement charges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is triggered by revenue, assets, shareholder count, or taxable activity for a non-resident Business Corporation. A compulsory audit applies only if the entity is listed on a recognised stock exchange, holds a banking or insurance licence under Marshall Islands law, or shareholders representing at least 10% of the voting power require an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; US GAAP is also acceptable for voluntarily prepared financial statements of a non-resident exempt corporation. There is no separately codified local GAAP for externally owned Business Corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO return is submitted to the Marshall Islands government. The registered agent must maintain the statutory registers and corporate records; share transfers must be authorised by the board or shareholders, recorded promptly in the Register of Members, and disclosed only in the annual report to the extent of share capital and principal members. There is no public beneficial-ownership register or annual UBO confirmation filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - 1,500 per year depending on the licensed registered agent and service level.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where no audit is statutorily triggered; voluntary certified review typically USD 1,500 - 4,000 and full audit USD 3,500 - 7,000 depending on transaction volume.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporations are exempt from Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) corporate income tax; RMI levies no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax, and no branch remittance tax. A 3% Business Privilege Tax applies only to local gross revenue sourced within RMI, which is not applicable to this offshore trading/manufacturing entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No RMI corporate income tax return is required for a non-resident Business Corporation. The sole compliance filing is the Annual Corporate Report filed through the RMI Online Filing System (Registrar of Corporations portal); Business Privilege Tax Form BPT-1 is only relevant if local-source gross revenue exceeds the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual corporate report in respect of the calendar year must be filed and the government registration fee paid no later than April 30 of the following year (or within the extension period allowed by the Registrar).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, registration number, registered agent name and registered office address in RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate non-resident status and provide registered agent details; no RMI tax number is required for tax-exempt non-resident entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, and citizenship of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; no RMI residency requirement applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and confirmation of no local RMI gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that the entity manufactures or sells custom double-shot PBT mechanical keyboard keycaps exclusively outside RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital, share classes, and beneficial ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital is required; beneficial owners must be disclosed to the registered agent but not publicly filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual corporate report incurs a penalty of 10% of the annual franchise fee per month or part thereof, plus potential striking-off of the company if filing remains outstanding for more than three months. Failure by the registered agent to maintain records attracts regulatory monetary fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreements with major trading partners; no treaty relief protocol or Tax Residency Certificate is required because RMI imposes no withholding tax on non-resident shareholders. Companies seeking to assert tax residence in RMI for foreign purposes should obtain a Certificate of Good Standing and, if necessary, a letter of tax status from the RMI Ministry of Finance, but such letters are of limited value due to RMI not levying income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 0%. There are no applicable treaty-reduced rates because RMI has no DTA network covering royalty and interest payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No RMI transfer pricing documentation threshold applies because RMI has no corporate income tax and no transfer pricing rules for non-resident Business Corporations. The 3% Business Privilege Tax applies only to locally sourced gross revenue; cross-border intercompany transactions with offshore suppliers or customers do not trigger a transfer pricing obligation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance Regulations apply to resident entities and non-resident entities registered in RMI carrying on 'relevant activities' (e.g., shipping, distribution and service center, holding company, finance and leasing). 'Double-shot PBT plastic injection manufacturing of keyboard keycaps' is not listed as a relevant activity in the Regulations, and the manufacturing activity is presumed to occur in a foreign operating subsidiary. Therefore, the entity is generally outside the scope of the RMI ESR reporting requirement, unless it also acts as a distribution or service center for related parties. If the entity only holds intercompany contracts without physical presence in RMI, it must ensure that substantive decisions and operational functions occur in the keycap manufacturing location to avoid shell-company characterization by overseas tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately reporting no RMI income while generating RMI-local-source revenue from physical sales, internet sales to RMI customers, or lease of property inside the Marshall Islands; or using the RMI entity as an opaque intermediary to conceal taxable profits from the beneficial owner's country of residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under RMI Business Privilege Tax law, evading Business Privilege Tax is punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 and imprisonment for up to three years, together with restitution of all unpaid taxes and penalties. Foreign jurisdictions may separately impose substantial tax fraud penalties and criminal charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly sign false declarations or participate in tax evasion may be held personally liable, including piercing of the corporate veil, personal fines, travel bans, seizure of assets, and imprisonment. Beneficial owners using the RMI BC to commit foreign tax fraud remain exposed to extradition and civil restitution claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a non-resident RMI Business Corporation without any local operational substance to manufacture custom mechanical keyboard caps solely for the purpose of treaty shopping, creating artificial losses, or sheltering income from foreign tax authorities while the actual production, procurement, and sales decisions occur in a high-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: While RMI itself does not penalize lack of economic substance for non-relevant activities, foreign tax authorities may recharacterize the arrangement under CFC rules, substance-based anti-abuse rules, or a general anti-avoidance rule, resulting in additional foreign taxes, interest, penalties of 50%-100% of the underpaid tax, and compulsory strike-off of the RMI entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the foreign operating parent can be jointly and severally liable for unwound transactions where the RMI entity had no commercial substance. Personal asset tracing, director disqualification orders, and potential criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payment via Shopify Payments or Stripe from sanctioned persons, failing to identify beneficial owners, or engaging in money laundering through the RMI entity tied to custom keyboard cap sales, including using the entity as a payment funnel for illicit proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI's Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism regime requires registered agents and financial institutions to file suspicious transaction reports. Offenders face fines up to $100,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Foreign correspondent banks may terminate banking relationships, and the entity may be blacklisted by financial action task force monitoring bodies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal fines, forfeiture of assets, travel restrictions, and criminal liability for failure to file SARs or for willful blindness to money laundering sourced through the e-commerce payment gateways.
